summary: Unexpected 502/503 surge caused by ephemeral keepalive FD exhaustion during mixed embed+chat burst
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme AI, dedicated) reported a sudden increase in 502/503s on their chat+embedding mixed route between 13:12-13:40 UTC. Symptoms: short-lived streaming sessions intermittently fail with 502; concurrent embedding bulk uploads receive 503s and large tail latencies.

Impact:
- ~12% error rate spike (502/503) observed for tenant traffic for ~25 minutes.
- Affected production customers using mixed streaming + embedding workflows; high user-visible error rate for chat features.

Environment:
- prod us-east-1, dedicated pool for Acme AI.
- Ingress via api-gateway -> ephemeral-proxy -> serving-runtime (tenant-shared).

Steps to reproduce (approximate):
1) Start a steady stream of long-lived streaming connections (1s keepalive interval) from many clients (~200 concurrent).
2) Trigger a large embedding bulk upload (~8k vectors, multiplexed into a few large requests) simultaneously.
3) Observe apigw accept-queue growth, ephemeral-proxy FD counts rising, followed by upstream runtime resets and 502/503 propagation.

Logs / Observations at time of spike:
- api-gateway metrics: accept_queue_depth > 800, connection_accept_latency p95 increased from 4ms -> 220ms.
- ephemeral-proxy process (proxy-ephemeral-12) reported file descriptor count ~62k (soft limit 65k) and transient EMFILE errors in logs.
- kernel dmesg showed repeated "too many open files" on ephemeral proxy host during peak.
- serving-runtime logs show watchog-triggered restart messages and "upstream connection reset by peer" prior to 502s.
- netstat/lsof snapshots captured large number of CLOSE_WAIT and LONG_ESTABLISHED websockets tied to a small set of client IPs.

Immediate customer-visible impact: 502/503s and increased first-byte latency for mixed-route calls.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 13:20 UTC - Support: Customer reported elevated 502s on mixed-route; collected request IDs and sample timestamps.
2026-03-13 13:22 UTC - SRE: Pulled apigw accept-queue, proxy fd usage, and runtime restart counts. Accept queue overflow correlated with FD saturation on ephemeral proxy node 'proxy-ephemeral-12'.
2026-03-13 13:25 UTC - Observation: Large embedding worker triggered high outbound connections to runtimes while streaming connections kept many fds open (keepalive misconfiguration).
2026-03-13 13:27 UTC - Hypothesis A: Ephemeral proxy reached OS soft FD limit resulting in EMFILE and failing accept() calls -> api-gateway returned 502s.
2026-03-13 13:28 UTC - Hypothesis B: Serving runtime watchdog restarted GPUs due to increased NVME IO from embedding checkpointing, compounding upstream restarts.

2026-03-13 13:31 UTC - Evidence: dmesg and proxy logs show EMFILE; runtime restarts coincident but error traces point at connection drops rather than OOM in runtime. More likely proxy accept failures first.
Tools/commands used: ss -s, lsof -p <proxy_pid> | wc -l, /proc/<pid>/limits, kubectl logs proxy-ephemeral-12, apigw metrics dashboard (AcceptQueue, p95_accept_latency).
Metric snapshots: ephemeral-proxy fd_usage 96% at 13:24 UTC, accept_queue_depth spike between 13:20-13:30 UTC, serving-runtime restart_count +6 within 10 minutes.
actions_taken: 2026-03-13 13:26 UTC: Scaled ephemeral-proxy replicas +3 in us-east to relieve accept queue. Immediate partial reduction in accept queue depth.
2026-03-13 13:30 UTC: Applied temporary connection culling rule to drop idle streaming connections > 350s for Acme tenant to free FDs.
2026-03-13 13:33 UTC: Increased OS soft ulimit (nofile) on affected ephemeral proxy hosts from 65536 -> 131072 as emergency mitigation.
2026-03-13 13:40 UTC: Applied backpressure to embedding ingestion (rate limit client-side via edge) to reduce burst concurrency. Error rate fell back to baseline over ~8 minutes.
Customer communication: Sent interim update and workaround steps at 13:36 UTC; customer acknowledged and applied client-side rate limiting for bulk upload.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) - 2026-03-13 13:18 UTC: Customer reported sudden chat failures and embedding timeouts. Collecting logs and request IDs.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-13 13:24 UTC: Seeing high fd usage on proxy-ephemeral-12 and EMFILE in proxy logs. Scaling proxies now.
Diego Morales (Platform Eng) - 2026-03-13 13:29 UTC: Noted runtime restarts but stack traces indicate connection resets. Prioritizing proxy remediation and ulimit bump.
Maya Patel (Support) - 2026-03-13 13:36 UTC: Customer applied temporary client-side rate limiting; errors decreasing. Customer asks for postmortem and permanent fix timeline.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-13 14:10 UTC: Confirming stabilized metrics after mitigation; monitoring for recurrence. Will open follow-ups for hardening.
resolution: Mitigated (temporary): scaled proxy replicas, increased per-host nofile soft limit, and applied tenant connection cull and client-side rate limiting. Error rate returned to baseline by 13:48 UTC. Root cause appears to be ephemeral-proxy file descriptor exhaustion driven by long-lived streaming connections combined with high-concurrency embedding bursts. Upstream runtime restarts were secondary, caused by connection churn.
follow_up_actions: Create infra ticket to add heuristics for automatic culling of stale streaming connections when FD usage exceeds threshold (INT-xxxxxx).
Permanent change: Raise default ephemeral-proxy nofile limits via bootstrap and add alert when fd_usage > 75% (owner: infra).
Add admission control for large embedding bulk uploads that detect concurrent long-lived streaming sessions and automatically stagger or queue requests (owner: serving-runtime).
Runbook update: Document mixed-workload acceptance criteria and emergency mitigation steps in Confluence runbook.
Postmortem: Draft and link a short postmortem summarizing timeline, root cause, and permanent remediation, target completion 2026-03-20.
notes: This incident surfaced an operational gap where long-lived websocket/streaming sessions together with DoS-ish embedding bursts can exhaust FD capacity on proxy nodes. Consider prioritizing work that adds headroom and smarter shedding for mixed routes.
